description:
STATUS (2026-09-14, main f26264572): LIVE NATIVE WRONG ANSWER, reproduced at every commit checked back to 4f49465f9. Interp is right. fz-3ai was filed for the same defect from a cold review of fz-21x.25 and is folded here.

MINIMAL WRONG-ANSWER REPRO (tail form):

    defp mk(n), do: {fn x -> x + n end, n}
    defp use({f, k}), do: f.(k)
    def main(), do: dbg(use(mk(5)))

interp: 10. JIT and AOT: a large run-dependent integer. Non-tail form (the original `apply_box({:a, make(1)}, 10)` -> `{:a, garbage}`) is the same defect through the Deliver flow. Control: the same lambda passed as a top-level parameter (`apply_fun(make(1), 10)`) is 11 on all three doors.

WHAT THE GARBAGE IS. Not the capture and not the argument: it is the RETURN. The value printed is an AnyValueRef word (tag 0xD = TAG_KIND_INT, address in the low bits) read as a RawInt. The CLIF of use/1 boxes the RawInt argument correctly before the tail call, then return_call_indirect into callable_wrapper_0 whose return repr is ValueRef, while use/1's own return repr is RawInt; nothing decodes the word.

VARIANTS (interp / JIT / AOT): no capture -> 5/5/5 green; capture only -> garbage; field order swapped, 3-field tuple, non-tail -> garbage; lambda returning int|float (caller return layout is itself one ValueRef lane) -> 10/10/10 GREEN, the cleanest proof that the mechanism is the return convention; lambda returning a bool -> garbage atom; lambda returning a 2-tuple -> hard abort in fz_closure_get_capture_ref; `use({f, _k}), do: f.(7)` -> refuses on all three doors with a zero-lane `callable(<unknown>/0 layouts=[])` field.

ROOT CAUSE. Three sites decide whether a closure call is direct or boxed and they are not the same question:
1. src/compiler2/jobs/artifact.rs ~1092 `public_callable = matches!(callee_layout.carrier, TransportCarrier::ValueRef(_))` (Direct edge minted when the carrier is not ValueRef);
2. src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs ~842 `TransportRecipe::ClosureCallReturn`, the same carrier predicate: the grounded branch gives the call a RawInt return layout instead of the PublicCallableReturn with_value_ref_carrier;
3. src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs `direct_closure_capture_lanes` (~4032-4092): "can I produce the target's capture lanes from the callee VALUE?"
For use/1, the callee value v1 has layout `lane(Value:fp[F] fun)` with carrier Absent: ValueRef is its lane REPR, not a TransportCarrier. So (1) and (2) answer "direct" (edge to x12 = lambda[int,int] -> RawInt, RawInt return layout) while (3) answers "no" (a bare lane publishes no capture lanes) and native silently downgrades to the boxed seam (`if !absent { return Ok(None) }`, then Term::TailCallClosure into the wrapper, x13, returning ValueRef). The two halves of one call were compiled against different executables.

WHY THE BACKSTOP MISSES IT. src/compiler2/backend_program/boxed_contract.rs ~50-55 `BoxedApplyRequirement::for_body` compares LANE COUNTS, never reprs, and exempts Tail/NoReturn entirely: the tail repro records no requirement at all; the Deliver repro has source reprs [RawInt] vs published [ValueRef], count 1 == 1, passes.

WHY THE TUPLE HOP LOSES THE DESCRIPTOR (second layer). use/1's input 0 demand settles to `whole callable(resolved=[] targets=[])`; exact_direct_callable_layout (transport.rs ~944-955) mints a ShapeDescr::Callable descriptor only when demand.callable.targets is non-empty, so a Whole tuple demand yields a plain `fun` lane, while the projected value v1 does carry `callable(resolved=[(int)] targets=[x12])`. The input position and the value it feeds disagree, so mk/1's return demand becomes first-class/escape and it boxes (construction=w0); the top-level control is `ignore ... direct=[(int)]`, construction=-, no closure object at all. NOT YET TRACED: the exact line where the field demand coarsens to Whole instead of TupleFields with populated callable targets.

FIX SHAPE.
Step 1 (correctness): one shared predicate for direct-vs-boxed over (callee TransportLayout, target ExecutableKey): "does the callee's settled layout publish this target's capture layouts", i.e. ShapeDescr::Callable(descr) with descr.function == target function; that is what direct_callable_captures already computes. artifact.rs and ClosureCallReturn read it; delete native's downgrade and the direct_ok bail-outs (~1560/1580/1589) so a mismatch is unrepresentable. Then use/1's call is classified boxed, its return layout is the ValueRef carrier, caller and seam agree by construction. Regression risk to check first: currently-green programs where the carrier predicate answers "direct" for a bare-lane capture-free callee.
Step 2 (north star, this ticket's title): propagate the projected value's callable targets to the tuple field's input demand so use/1 publishes field 0 as callable(mk/1#lambda@0/1/1 layouts=[lane(int)]) like the control; mk/1 then never boxes and the call is a real direct call. `use({f, _k}), do: f.(7)` shows TupleFields alone is not enough: the field's callable axis must carry the resolved target.
Step 3 (honest backstop): BoxedApplyRequirement::for_body compares callable_return_reprs(wrapper.return_form) against the caller's expected reprs and stops exempting Tail/NoReturn (a Tail boxed call requires the caller's own return layout to equal the seam's form).
Docs: .agent/docs/pipeline.md ~579-617 states the rule in terms of the ValueRef carrier; restate it as the shared predicate, and "either half alone is an abort" becomes "with matching lane counts it is a silent wrong answer".

RED TESTS FIRST. Behavior fixture tuple_field_closure_call (the tail repro, `.oracle.exs`, expected 10) plus one case per return repr across the seam (RawInt, RawAtom, 2-tuple, capture-only, field-swap, 3-field, the int|float control) and the Deliver form; a boxed_contract.rs unit test that a Tail caller over a value_ref callee records a requirement and a [RawInt] caller mismatches a ValueRef wrapper; a transport_contract_test producer/consumer agreement test for the field layout mk/1 publishes vs use/1 declares. No fixture today puts a lambda in a tuple and calls it after destructuring.

Related: fz-kdt.159 (same lane-count comparison hole in BoxedContracts), fz-kdt.154 (return flow authority per door), fz-kdt.160.

TRACE OF THE SECOND LAYER (2026-09-14, verified at f26264572). The field demand DOES carry the target: closure_callee_demand (runtime_demand.rs ~2408-2459) puts targets=[x12] on the projected value v1, and the LoweredStep::TupleField arm (~1799-1807) forwards the full RuntimeDemand into TupleFields{0: ...}. It is then destroyed by the JOIN: the arm guesses the tuple arity as `asserted_tuple_arities.get(source).unwrap_or(index + 1)` and a clause-head pattern on a statically known tuple emits no AssertTuple, so `v1 = tuple_field v0.0` contributes TupleFields([callable]) (arity 1) and `v2 = tuple_field v0.1` contributes TupleFields([ignore, whole]) (arity 2); ShapeDemand::join (semantic.rs ~386-389) answers Whole for vectors of different length, and every callable axis nested inside the field vector dies with it. The doc comments at semantic.rs ~405 and ~472 ("coarsening the shape cannot erase callable obligations") are true at depth 0 and false at depth 1. Proof: the same program written with a body match (`{f, k} = t`) emits assert_tuple arity=2, both projections agree, and the settled input is `fields(ignore callable(resolved=[(int)] targets=[x12]), whole)`.

Hole #2, independent: even with the target on the field, the exact callable layout is unreachable at field depth. exact_direct_callable_layout (transport.rs ~944-982) is called only from TransportRecipe::Terminal (~826) for a whole position; field layouts go joined_tuple_structural -> joined_transport_layout -> generic_layout_from_demand (~2409), whose callable arm calls generic_callable_shape_with_resolutions (~2497-2512) which discards `_demand` and interns `function: None, capture_layouts: []`. That is the `callable(<unknown>/0 layouts=[])` zero-lane field behind the three-door refusal of `use({f, _k}), do: f.(7)`. Note exact_direct_callable_layout can return RecipeLayout::Waiting, which the field recursion cannot express today.

SMALLEST CHANGE. (i) ShapeDemand::TupleFields is already a PREFIX encoding on the consumer side (transport.rs tuple_field_demands accepts fields.len() <= arity and pads with ignore); make the join pad the shorter side with ignore and join pointwise, deleting the Whole arm for unequal lengths. That cures every index+1 guess at once. (ii) Make generic_layout_from_demand's callable arm try exact_direct_callable_layout first and fall back to the generic shape, the exact-then-generic order Terminal already uses; the field recursion must propagate Waiting. Unverified until built: direct_callable_descr resolving the capture position for a field-depth TransportPosition. With both, mk/1's return becomes callable(mk/1#lambda@0/1/1 layouts=[lane(int)]) reprs=[RawInt], construction=-, no closure, and the call is a real direct call to x12.

STEP 1 REGRESSION SURFACE. Readers of the carrier predicate: artifact.rs ~1092 (authority), transport.rs ~843 (mirrors it), boxed_contract.rs ~46; divergent implementations of a different question: native.rs direct_closure_capture_lanes (~4032-4102) and ir_interp/backend.rs ~1141-1185. Across all 31 fixtures that call a variable, 82 Direct edges all have a callable(...) layout naming a function and 40 Indirect edges all have carrier ValueRef; zero fixture edges have a bare lane(fun) callee, so the bare-lane shape is reachable only through the tuple-field path and the checked-in regression surface of Step 1 is empty. Capture-free lambdas in a tuple (`fn x -> x end`) are green today and must stay Direct: the shared predicate is "the caller can supply every capture input the target declares", satisfied by (a) ShapeDescr::Callable naming the target, or (b) the target declaring no captures (the vacuous case; direct_closure_capture_lanes already has this two-case shape at ~4059-4076 / ~4077-4102). capture_count is published per activation (executable_facts.rs ~250-268), so the artifact layer can answer it. The shared calculator is the DECISION half (pure over callee layout + target activation); native keeps the emission.

comments.text:
STILL RED at fz-kdt.119's head (4ca1dc7e7), as expected -- 119 did not touch it and this ticket still owns it. One symptom MOVED, so the reproducer's error text in this ticket is now stale:

  refnest.fz  (the {tag, f} = box destructure through a forwarding hop)
    base  b32d645ac: 'native executable lowering failed for index 13'
    head  4ca1dc7e7: 'native cannot project captures out of a callable that
                      names no function in Executable(... FunctionId(66) ...)'
  refnest2.fz: unchanged, still fails all three doors.

Same failure, one layer earlier: the callable-identity envelope now reaches the nested position (that is 119's item 3), so the nested callable is named where it used to be widened, and the lowering refuses at capture projection rather than at the end. Neither compiles, so 119's REFNEST acceptance probe stayed unconstructible exactly as this ticket said.

CONSEQUENCE HONOURED: 119's nested-callable separation is gated by UNIT tests at the dispatch layer instead --
  callsite_dispatch::tests::a_closure_nested_in_a_tuple_is_named_by_the_test
  callsite_dispatch::tests::a_nested_callables_captures_are_not_a_question
-- which pin both halves of the law (two callables one tuple deep are two disjoint questions; one callable at two capture layouts is ONE question, joining fz-kdt.127's population). When this ticket lands, those claims want the three-door fixture the probes were meant to be.

RE-TESTED at 29b07acfa (after fz-kdt.127.1 + .2, 2026-09-02): STILL RED, unchanged in kind. refnest.fz: interp correct ({:a, 11} {:a, 30}); native refuses 'native cannot project captures out of a callable that names no function in Executable(... FunctionId(66) ...)' then 'native executable lowering failed for index 13'. refnest2.fz (pattern-destructured): interp 'backend executable 11 function 65 clause 0 failed before entry 0: backend value 0 is unbound'; native same refusal. Neither stage of 127 touched the nested-in-tuple capture projection; the closures here capture nothing, so the forwarder key still erases them to the bare arrow inside the tuple (capture-free literals erase whole), and the refusal is the transport/projection of a callable position INSIDE a tuple through an erased hop. Still this ticket's. Note for whoever picks it up: 127.2's anonymous literal closure[?](caps) also 'names no function' -- a capture-BEARING closure nested in a tuple through a forwarder would meet the same refusal one form later; add that variant to the reproducers.

Draft PR https://github.com/jallum/fz/pull/169 (commit c423f52f7 on fz-kdt.137/closure-in-tuple-field off main f26264572). Two cold-review passes: one blocker (tuple used whole after destructure-and-call refused with a panic) fixed via layout_is_one_public_word; all must-fixes applied. Full gate green (lib 2134/0, matrix 765/0 single-threaded, oracle trial). Side ticket fz-b54 filed.

PR #169 amended to 47e7502f4: the six tests this ticket adds now live in sibling _test.rs files (semantic_test.rs, backend_program/boxed_contract_test.rs, jobs/artifact_test.rs, ir_interp/backend_test.rs) per the new rule; lib 2134/0 unchanged.

title: P1: native loses callable identity and captures when invoking a closure projected from a tuple
